simple.explanation: 5 The Frog Let us Recite I sit in ponds and in the rain, Or hop about in a muddy drain.
As a tadpole, I swim with cheer, A tiny fish-like thing, so clear!
I flick my tongue to catch my food, It works so fast—now that’s quite good!
I live on land and water too, In places damp with drops of dew.
My colours match the plants and trees, I hide so well in grass and leaves!
But snakes are near, I must beware, Or else they’ll catch me unaware!
I croak my songs, they sound so loud, Yet in my pond, I feel so proud.
I hop around, I jump so high, Up I go into the sky!
With webbed feet, I swim with ease, And leap so high in joyful breeze!
Where does the frog like to sit or spend time?
What helps the frog hide in its surroundings?
What would it feel like to live like a frog, both in water and on land?
If you could hop as high as a frog, what fun things would you do?
How is a frog’s life different from a fish’s life?
How are frogs’ webbed feet similar to the flippers used by scuba divers?
New Words hop muddy flick damp dew beware croak webbed

Would you like to learn about frogs ............... tadpoles? (because/and) 3.
Frogs swim easily ............... they have webbed feet. (because/or) B.
The following words have been rearranged into sentences.
1. hunts/night/the/silently/tiger/at Options: a.
2. elephants/in/forests/live/large/ groups/in Options: a.
In groups large, elephants live in forests. c.
58 Santoor Grade 5 3. web/a/spider/carefully/its/weaves Options: a.
4. crocodile/waits/the/silently/riverbank/ the/near Options: a.
Crocodile waits the silently the near riverbank. b.
The silently crocodile waits near the riverbank. c.
The crocodile waits silently near the riverbank.
5. a/swims/turtle/slowly/in/ocean/the Options: a.
Try speaking each tongue twister slowly at first.
Gradually increase your speed with each repetition.
Count how many times you can say it correctly without making a mistake.
Listen and repeat Your teacher will say aloud the following pairs of words.
Listen carefully and repeat each pair. bet bat set sat men man leg lag met mat Note to the Teacher • Say aloud every pair of words.
Ensure that learners pronounce it clearly. • Do this exercise at regular and frequent intervals.
My Frog’s World Your teacher will read out instructions for you to follow and create your own ‘Frog’s World’ in the space provided on the next page.
Draw the place: Imagine a place where your frog might be happy, like a pond, a forest or a rainy area.
Draw your frog: Draw a frog in the above setting.
Decorate with words: Around your drawing, write some words from the poem that describe the frog’s life.
You can even write your own short sentence about the frog’s world.
60 Santoor Grade 5 Note to the Teacher Read the instructions given in the ‘Let us Listen’ section, adding details of your own.
For example, the first instruction may include details like trees, shrubs, plants, water, etc.
Similarly, for the second you may elaborate on its webbed feet, its colour, and even its tongue, catching food.
Colour it: Use colours to bring your frog’s world to life!
Be creative and make it as colourful as you would like.
61 The Frog Here is a message for you from Hopper, the frog.
I am writing this message to you from my big lily leaf pad.
My favourite hobby is sitting in water puddles and croaking.
Your friend, Hopper Write a reply to Hopper in your notebook and share it with your class.
